headline: Multi-omics gene prioritization nominates candidate hub genes across diverse diseases
label: Integrative Transcriptomic Gene Prioritization
summary: Combining public transcriptomic cohorts, single-cell data and Mendelian randomization now yields prioritized candidate genes across many disease contexts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is transcriptomic profiling of diseased tissue followed by computational prioritization that narrows large gene sets to candidate hubs. TIMP1 in autoimmune gastritis and gastric cancer was nominated using LASSO, random forest, PPI and scRNA-seq; MET and SELL in endometriosis were linked to gut microbiota metabolites via PPI, SHAP and single-cell data; ELF2 in vascular dementia was derived from bulk and single-cell transcriptomes. Mendelian randomization layers appear in several items, including COPD and periodontitis and MAFF in Parkinson's disease. Not every item applies the full stack: the CCL26 study adds experimental validation, while the CA2 study in atopic dermatitis pairs scRNA-seq perturbation analysis with docking and molecular dynamics. What is new is the breadth of this workflow across gut, gastric, reproductive, airway, skin, ocular and neurological contexts.
